rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses objected to Gabriel's call for gentleness because the magicians sought to defeat the miracle and support Pharaoh's religion; Gabriel said they would be with Moses until afternoon prayer and then in Paradise.
rows.anchor: يا موسى ترفق بأولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses wondered whether God's knowledge of him might differ from his present state, as it had with the magicians; God then reassured him not to fear.
rows.anchor: فلعلي أكون الآن في حالة، وعلم الله في على خلافها كما كان هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is highest in that he prevails over the magicians in this world and holds the highest ranks in Paradise through prophethood and God's choosing him.
rows.anchor: أي الغالب لهم في الدنيا، وفي الدرجات العلا في الجنة للنبوة والاصطفاء الذي آتاك الله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original form of khīfa is khawfa; the waw changed to ya because the kha has kasra.
rows.anchor: وأصل «خيفة» خوفة فانقلبت الواو ياء لانكسار الخاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not naming the staff may diminish it rhetorically: Moses should disregard the many ropes and staffs and cast the small, solitary stick, which by God's power will swallow them.
rows.anchor: فجائز أن تكون تصغيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the omission magnifies the staff: the many large objects are negligible beside what Moses holds, which will erase them by God's permission.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون تعظيما لها أي لا تحفل بهذه الأجرام الكثيرة الكبيرة فإن في يمينك شيئا أعظم منها كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talaqqaf in the jussive answers the imperative, with an understood condition: if you cast it, it will swallow them; the verb means to take and swallow.
rows.anchor: و«تلقف» بالجزم جواب الأمر كأنه قال: إن تلقه تتلقف أي تأخذ وتبتلع

rows.speaker: السلمي وحفص
rows.claim: Al-Sulami and Hafs read talaqqaf with a quiescent lam, from laqifa yalqafu.
rows.anchor: وقرأ السلمي وحفص «تلقف» ساكنة اللام من لقف يلقف لقفا.

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان وأبو حيوة الشامي ويحيى بن الحرث
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Haywa al-Shami, and Yahya ibn al-Harith read with the ta deleted and the fa nominative, meaning the staff itself swallows.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن ذكوان وأبو حيوة الشامي ويحيى بن الحرث «تلقف» بحذف التاء ورفع الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative may address Moses or, alternatively, the staff.
rows.anchor: والخطاب لموسى. وقيل: للعصا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laqf is taking something quickly; the expression also describes a quick, deft person.
rows.anchor: يقال: لقفت الشيء بالكسر ألقفه لقفا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub gives laqif thaqif as an expression for a quick, capable, deft man.
rows.anchor: عن يعقوب: يقال رجل لقف ثقف أي خفيف حاذق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laqf can also mean a wall falling; a basin may cave in at its base and widen. Talaqqafa, talaqqama, and talahhama are synonymous for swallowing.
rows.anchor: واللقف بالتحريك سقوط الحائط. ولقد لقف الحوض لقفا أي تهور من أسفله واتسع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma ṣanaʿū and innamā ṣanaʿū refer to what they made.
rows.anchor: أي الذي صنعوه وكذا { إنما صنعوا } أي إن الذي صنعوه

rows.speaker: الكوفيون إلا عاصما
rows.claim: The Kufans except Asim read kaydu in the nominative and siḥr with kasra on sin and sukun on ha.
rows.anchor: كيد } بالرفع «سحر» بكسر السين وإسكان الحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nominative reading, kayd may be annexed to siḥr without ellipsis, or an omitted phrase may mean a plot belonging to a possessor of magic.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون الكيد مضافا إلى السحر على الإتباع من غير تقدير حذف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers put kayd in the accusative as the object of ṣanaʿū; mā is restrictive, no pronoun is elided before sāḥir, and kayd is truly annexed to the magician.
rows.anchor: بوقوع الصنع عليه، و«ما» كافة ولا تضمر هاء «ساحر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza of anna may be opened with causal force: because what they made is a magician's plot.
rows.anchor: ويجوز فتح «أن» على معنى لأن ما صنعوا كيد ساحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magician does not succeed or escape wherever he comes from on earth; alternatively, wherever he schemes.
rows.anchor: أي لا يفوز ولا ينجو حيث أتى من الأرض. وقيل: حيث احتال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers readers to al-Baqara for the ruling on magicians and the meaning of magic.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «البقرة» حكم الساحر ومعنى السحر فتأمله هناك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians prostrated at the extraordinary power they witnessed: the staff swallowed their ropes and sticks, a load of three hundred camels, then returned to being a staff; only God knew where the objects went.
rows.anchor: فإنها ابتلعت جميع ما احتالوا به من الحبال والعصي وكانت حمل ثلاثمائة بعير ثم عادت عصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points back to al-Aʿraf for this account of the staff and its swallowing the magicians' devices.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في «الأعراف» هذا المعنى وأمر العصا مستوفى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āmantum lahu means that they believed in him; Arabic also uses āmana bihi, as in the verse about Lot.
rows.anchor: قال آمنتم له } أي به يقال: آمن له وآمن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites the verse about Lot as an example of āmana lahu, believing in someone.
rows.anchor: فآمن له لوط [العنكبوت: 26]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question rebukes the magicians for transgressing and acting without his permission.
rows.anchor: إنكار منه عليهم أي تعديتم وفعلتم ما لم آمركم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh falsely called Moses their chief and teacher to confuse the people and prevent them from following the magicians' faith; Pharaoh knew they learned magic before Moses arrived or was born.
rows.anchor: وإنما أراد فرعون بقوله هذا ليشبه على الناس حتى لا يتبعوهم فيؤمنوا كإيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh threatens to cut off opposite hands and feet and crucify them on palm trunks.
rows.anchor: أيديكم وأرجلكم من خلاف ولأصلبنكم في جذوع النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the trunks means on the trunks; Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil's verse attests crucifixion on a palm trunk.
rows.anchor: هم صلبوا العبدي في جذع نخلة فلا عطست شيبان إلا بأجدعا

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads both forms here and in al-Aʿraf with an open hamza and lighter consonant doubling, from the forms qataʿa and ṣalaba.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن هنا وفي الأعراف «فلأقطعن»، و«لأصلبنكم» بفتح الألف والتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By asking which gives harsher and more lasting punishment, Pharaoh means himself or the Lord of Moses.
rows.anchor: يعني أنا أم رب موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians were cut and crucified until they died; the author invokes mercy for them.
rows.anchor: فقطع وصلب حتى ماتوا رحمهم الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses held Aaron's hair in his right hand and beard in his left, overcome by zeal for God; Aaron asks him to stop lest people think it contempt or punishment.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: أخذ شعره بيمينه ولحيته بيساره لأن الغيرة في الله ملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Moses acted neither contemptuously nor as punishment, but handled Aaron's beard as one might handle one's own; God knows the Prophet's intent.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن موسى عليه السلام إنما فعل هذا على غير استخفاف ولا عقوبة

words: إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel: leaving with Moses would split the people between him and the calf, and could cause bloodshed.
rows.anchor: أي خشيت أن أخرج وأتركهم وقد أمرتني أن أخرج معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron also feared that if he restrained the people and fighting resulted, Moses would blame him; this answers Moses' question about disobeying his command.
rows.anchor: وخشيت إن زجرتهم أن يقع قتال فتلومني على ذلك. وهذا جواب هارون لموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron's explanation is connected to his plea in al-Aʿraf that Israel had overpowered him and nearly killed him, and Moses had ordered him to remain with them.
rows.anchor: إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil explains lam tarqub qawli as failing to act on Moses' instruction to preserve the people by staying among them.
rows.anchor: لأنك أمرتني أن أكون معهم قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains the phrase as not waiting for Moses' covenant or arrival.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: لم تنتظر عهدي وقدومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭb means one's affair or situation, and here asks what drove the Samiri to do what he did.
rows.anchor: وما الذي حملك على ما صنعت؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Samiri was prominent in Israel, from a tribe called Samira, but became a hypocrite after crossing the sea; he exploited their attraction to idols and made the calf after they asked Moses for a god.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كان السامري عظيما في بني إسرائيل من قبيلة يقال لها سامرة

rows.speaker: السامري
rows.claim: The Samiri claimed he saw Gabriel on a living horse and seized some of its trace; whatever he cast it on gained life, flesh, and blood, and his soul then tempted him to make the calf.
rows.anchor: رأيت جبريل عليه السلام على فرس الحياة، فألقي في نفسي أن أقبض من أثره قبضة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that when Gabriel descended to take Moses up to heaven, the Samiri alone among the people saw him and took a handful from the horse's trace.
rows.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: لما نزل جبريل ليصعد بموسى عليه السلام إلى السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the Samiri saw Gabriel riding a horse whose steps reached as far as sight, and casting its trace on something gave it life and blood.
rows.anchor: وقيل قال السامري: رأيت جبريل على الفرس وهي تلقي خطوها مد البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says he saw Gabriel on an eager mare as it went ahead of Pharaoh's cavalry into the sea.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رأى جبريل يوم نزل على رمكة وديق، فتقدم خيل فرعون في ورود البحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further story says the Samiri's mother hid him in a cave from Pharaoh; Gabriel fed him honey and milk, so the Samiri recognized him later.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن أم السامري جعلته حين وضعته في غار خوفا من أن يقتله فرعون فجاءه جبريل

words: وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِۦٓ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase not to extend one's eyes toward what people enjoy was explained earlier in al-Ḥijr.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم معناه في «الحجر».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan is the object of mattaʿnā.
rows.anchor: مفعول ب«متعنا». و { زهرة } نصب على الحال.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses zahrah as an object in meaning because mattaʿnā means God made worldly life a flower for them, or supplies an omitted jaʿalnā.
rows.anchor: «زهرة» منصوبة بمعنى «متعنا» لأن معناه جعلنا لهم الحياة الدنيا زهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view makes zahrah a substitute for the pronoun in bihi by its syntactic position, as in marartu bihi akhāka.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي بدل من الهاء في «به» على الموضع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses zahrah as a circumstantial accusative governed by mattaʿnā, estimating that God gave them it as flower and adornment in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وأشار الفراء إلى نصبه على الحال والعامل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parsing zahrah as a cognate accusative, like ṣunʿ Allāh or waʿd Allāh, is possible but weak in the author's view.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب على المصدر مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best parse makes zahrah a circumstantial accusative, omitting tanwin at the lām; al-ḥayāh is genitive as a substitute for mā, giving the sense of the world's life in its flowering state.
rows.anchor: مخفوضة على البدل من «ما»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making zahrah a substitute for mā at its syntactic position does not work because linatnahum depends on mattaʿnā.
rows.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يكون «زهرة» بدلا من «ما» على الموضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zahrah al-ḥayāh al-dunyā means the world's adornment in vegetation; zahrah with open vowels means a plant's flower, while ẓuhrah with ḍamma on zāy means a star.
rows.anchor: زهرة الحياة الدنيا } يعني زينتها بالنبات

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads zahrah with an open ha, by analogy with nahr and nahr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر «زهرة» بفتح الهاء

rows.speaker: ابن عزيز
rows.claim: Ibn Aziz notes that Banū Zuhra has a quiescent ha; zāhir describes a shining lamp, and flowers are named for their pleasing colors.
rows.anchor: وبنو زهرة بسكون الهاء قاله ابن عزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is described as azhar al-lawn, luminous in complexion; zāhir is used of anything shining and this is the finest color.
rows.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أزهر اللون أي نير اللون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linatnahum fīhi means to test them with worldly enjoyment, or to make it a temptation and misguidance for them.
rows.anchor: لنجعل ذلك فتنة لهم وضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should assign no lasting worth to worldly adornment because it does not endure.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: لا تجعل يا محمد لزهرة الدنيا وزنا، فإنه لا بقاء لها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to stretch one's eyes is stronger than a command merely not to look: prolonged gaze implies desire and greed, while looking need not.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي يمد بصره، إنما يحمله على ذلك حرص مقترن، والذي ينظر

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Some attributed the occasion of revelation to Abu Rafi's report about a guest who came to the Prophet and his request for flour or a loan from a Jewish man.
rows.anchor: سبب نزول هذه الآية ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of Abu Rafi's report says the Jew would sell or lend only with collateral; the Prophet sent his armor and said he would repay.
rows.anchor: نزل بنا ضيف ولم يلف عندنا بعض الذي يصلحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the verse was revealed to console the Prophet about worldly life.
rows.anchor: ونزلت الآية تعزية له عن الدنيا.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects this as the occasion of revelation because the sura is Meccan while the story is Medinan, late in the Prophet's life, when he died with his armor pawned to a Jew.
rows.anchor: وهذا معترض أن يكون سببا لأن السورة مكية والقصة المذكورة مدنية

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya instead reads the verse in context: after rebuking failure to learn from past peoples and threatening delayed punishment, God tells the Prophet to discount their wealth and endure their words because it will end in disgrace.
rows.anchor: أن الآية متناسقة مع ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author relates that the Prophet passed camels of Banu al-Mustaliq, covered in their dung and urine from fatness, covered himself with his garment, and moved on in response to the verse.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ما روي عنه عليه السلام أنه مر بإبل بني المصطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward for patience and indifference to worldly life is better because it lasts while the world perishes.
rows.anchor: أي ثواب الله على الصبر وقلة المبالاة بالدنيا أولى لأنه يبقى والدنيا تفنى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes God's provision to mean the lands and spoils He will open for believers.
rows.anchor: يعني بهذا الرزق ما يفتح الله على المؤمنين من البلاد والغنائم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to order his family to pray, to pray with them himself, and to persevere; the address includes the whole community, with his household specially included.
rows.anchor: أمره تعالى بأن يأمر أهله بالصلاة ويمتثلها معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this verse was revealed, the Prophet went each morning to Fatima and Ali's home and called them to prayer.
rows.anchor: وكان عليه السلام بعد نزول هذه الآية يذهب كل صباح إلى بيت فاطمة وعلي رضوان الله عليهما

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: When Urwa ibn al-Zubayr saw reports about rulers, he hurried home, recited the verse through wa-abqā, called his household to prayer, and prayed.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن عروة بن الزبير رضي الله عنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من أخبار السلاطين وأحوالهم بادر إلى منزله فدخله

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab woke his household for night prayer, prayed, and invoked this verse.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يوقظ أهل داره لصلاة الليل ويصلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself and his family or neglect prayer for income; God guarantees their provision, and in household hardship the Prophet told them to pray.
rows.anchor: لا نسألك أن ترزق نفسك وإياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links God's assurance of provision to His declaration that He created jinn and humans to worship, asks no provision from them, and is the Provider.
rows.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون * ما أريد منهم من رزق وما أريد أن يطعمون إن الله هو الرزاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good end for the God-fearing is Paradise; others may have an outcome, but it is blameworthy and so as if nonexistent.
rows.anchor: أي الجنة لأهل التقوى يعني العاقبة المحمودة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud calls al-Kahf, Maryam, Ṭā Hā, and al-Anbiya among the earliest suras he acquired, likening old memorized material to inherited wealth.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: الكهف ومريم وطه والأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Companion building a wall on the day this sura was revealed stopped when told the reckoning was near, declaring he would never build again.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رجلا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يبني جدارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning has drawn near means that the time for people to be called to account for their deeds is close.
rows.anchor: «اقترب» أي قرب الوقت الذي يحاسبون فيه على أعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people here are the polytheists, as shown by the following description of them listening in play and calling the message magic.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: المراد بالناس هاهنا المشركون بدليل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, people is general, although Quraysh were the immediate referent, as the following verses indicate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الناس عموم وإن كان المشار إليه في ذلك الوقت كفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing the Hour is near should shorten one's hopes, turn one to repentance, and loosen attachment to the world: the past is gone, every future is near, each person's death is his own Hour, and little of the world's time remains compared with what passed.
rows.anchor: ومن علم اقتراب الساعة قصر أمله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains their reckoning as punishment: Meccans had dismissed the promised punishment as delayed, and their defeat came at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: معنى { اقترب للناس حسابهم } أي عذابهم

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says one cannot say iqtaraba ḥisābuhum lil-nās, because an implicit element cannot precede an explicit one when meant to be delayed.
rows.anchor: النحاس: ولا يجوز في الكلام اقترب حسابهم للناس لئلا يتقدم مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is an independent report; outside the Qur'anic reading it could be accusative as a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: ويجوز النصب في غير القرآن على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says they are absorbed in worldly life and turn away from the afterlife.
rows.anchor: «وهم في غفلة معرضون» يعني بالدنيا عن الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says they neglect preparing for the reckoning and turn away from what Muhammad brought.
rows.anchor: عن التأهب للحساب وعما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the waw as equivalent to idh, the circumstantial waw, as in the example from al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: وهذه الواو عند سيبويه بمعنى «إذ» وهي التي يسميها النحويون واو الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Khuzaa, who said angels were God's daughters and worshipped them in hope of their intercession.
rows.anchor: يعبدونهم طمعا في شفاعتهم لهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Maʿmar's report from Qatada says Jews, or some groups in Maʿmar's recension, attributed affinity with jinn to God and said angels were from the jinn.
rows.anchor: وروى معمر عن قتادة قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥānah declares God exalted above the claim that He has a child.
rows.anchor: فقال الله عز وجل: «سبحانه» تنزيها له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are honored servants, not children as the disbelievers alleged.
rows.anchor: بل عباد } أي بل هم عباد { مكرمون } أي ليس كما زعم هؤلاء الكفار

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj permits the accusative, with the sense that God took honored servants instead.
rows.anchor: ويجوز النصب عند الزجاج على معنى بل اتخذ عبادا مكرمين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also permits the accusative by coordinating ʿibādan with walad: God did not take them as children but as honored servants.
rows.anchor: وأجازه الفراء على أن يرده على ولد، أي بل لم نتخذهم ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walad can denote one or many, or can be a collective noun, like māl.
rows.anchor: والولد هاهنا للجمع، وقد يكون الواحد والجمع ولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not speak before God speaks; they say only what He commands and act in obedience to His orders.
rows.anchor: ولا يتكلمون إلا بما يأمرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains what is before and behind them as what they have done and what they will do.
rows.anchor: ما عملوا وما هم عاملون قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second explanation from Ibn Abbas takes what is before them as the Hereafter and what is behind them as the world; al-Thaʿlabi transmits the first and al-Qushayri the second.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس. وعنه أيضا: { ما بين أيديهم } الآخرة { وما خلفهم } الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says those God approves for intercession are people who testify that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم أهل شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the angels intercede only for everyone with whom God is pleased.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هم كل من رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels intercede in the Hereafter, as established in sound reports, and in this world by asking forgiveness for believers and earth's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: والملائكة يشفعون غدا في الآخرة كما في صحيح مسلم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are fearful of God and do not feel secure against His plan.
rows.anchor: أي خائفون لا يأمنون مكره.

words: وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌۭ مِّن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وغيرهما
rows.claim: Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others say the claimant is Iblis, who claimed partnership and called people to worship him; no other angel claimed divinity.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك وغيرهما: عنى بهذه الآية إبليس حيث ادعى الشركة

words: وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌۭ مِّن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the warning may refer to any angel who makes such a claim, who would be punished with Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإشارة إلى جميع الملائكة

words: وَمَن يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّىٓ إِلَٰهٌۭ مِّن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that even though angels are protected from sin, they are commanded to worship rather than compelled, contrary to the ignorant view.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أنهم وإن أكرموا بالعصمة فهم متعبدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas uses this verse to argue that Muhammad is the best of the inhabitants of heaven; the issue was discussed earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل ابن عباس بهذه الآية على أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل أهل السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers are those who put divinity and worship where they do not belong, and God punishes them likewise.
rows.anchor: أي كما جزينا هذا بالنار فكذلك نجزي الظالمين الواضعين الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadab means raised ground and its plural is ḥidāb, derived from the hump of the back; Antara's line attests the plural.
rows.anchor: والحدب ما ارتفع من الأرض، والجمع الحداب مأخوذ من حدبة الظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of yansilūn is that they emerge; Imruʾ al-Qays uses tansalu as evidence for that sense.
rows.anchor: فسلي ثيابي من ثيابك تنسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they hurry: al-Nabigha's line uses nasala of a wolf's swift movement, and al-ʿasal means to walk quickly.
rows.anchor: عسلان الذئب أمسى قاربا برد الليل عليه فنسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith expression means to walk quickly; al-Zajjaj calls naslan a wolf's fast gait.
rows.anchor: أي عليك بسرعة المشي. وقال الزجاج: والنسلان مشية الذئب إذا أسرع

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nasala means to run fast; the verb has forms with kasra or ḍamma and several verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: يقال: نسل فلان في العدو ينسل بالكسر والضم نسلا ونسولا ونسلانا أي أسرع

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
rows.claim: The strongest view, also held by Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas, identifies those rushing from every height as Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: وهو الأظهر وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them with all creatures, gathered toward the plain of assembly and hurrying from every direction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جميع الخلق فإنهم يحشرون إلى أرض الموقف

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد وأبو الصهباء
rows.claim: An anomalous reading has min kulli jadath, graves, instead of ḥadab; al-Mahdawi transmits it from Ibn Masud and al-Thaʿlabi from Mujahid and Abu al-Sahba, echoing Yasin.
rows.anchor: وحكى هذه القراءة المهدوي عن ابن مسعود والثعلبي عن مجاهد وأبي الصهباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { واقترب الوعد الحق }

rows.speaker: الفراء والكسائي وغيرهما
rows.claim: Al-Farra, al-Kisaʾi, and others treat the waw as extra: when Gog and Magog are opened, the true promise approaches, and fa-iqtaraba answers idhā.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء والكسائي وغيرهما: الواو زائدة مقحمة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites poetry where waw is extra, and compares the Qur'anic phrase wa-tallahū lil-jabīn wa-nādaynāhu, understood as tallahū lil-jabīn nādaynāhu.
rows.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء:
فلما أجزنا ساحة الحي وانتحى

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi allows fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun to answer idhā, with iqtaraba al-waʿd al-ḥaqq coordinated to the conditional verb.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي أن يكون جواب

rows.speaker: البصريون والزجاج
rows.claim: The Basran grammarians, including al-Zajjaj, say the answer is omitted, with an estimate such as qālū yā waylanā; the author calls this a sound view.
rows.anchor: وقال البصريون: الجواب محذوف والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted speech is supported by the common deletion of qālū, as in the verse about those who worship intermediaries and say they seek nearness to God.
rows.anchor: قالوا ما نعبدهم، وحذف القول كثير

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hiya refers to the eyes, and the following word abṣār explains it: when the promise comes, the eyes of disbelievers stare.
rows.anchor: «هي» ضمير الأبصار، والأبصار المذكورة بعدها تفسير لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet's use of hiya before later naming the she-camel is cited as evidence for a pronoun whose referent appears afterward.
rows.anchor: لعمر أبيها لا تقول ظعينتي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra treats hiya as a supporting pronoun, as in the verse saying that it is not the eyes that go blind.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: «هي» عماد، مثل

words: فَإِذَا هِىَ شَٰخِصَةٌ أَبْصَٰرُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the statement ends at hiya, meaning the Resurrection is present; the next clause front-loads its predicate, with the disbelievers' eyes staring from terror and scarcely blinking.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الكلام تم عند قوله: «هي» التقدير: فإذا هي بمعنى القيامة

words: يَٰوَيْلَنَا قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا بَلْ كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers cry woe because of the day's terror, admitting wrongdoing through disobedience and misplacing worship.
rows.anchor: من هذا اليوم أي من هوله لا تكاد تطرف

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse argues for resurrection from the first creation, and its conditional wording challenges the hearer to consider that proof.
rows.anchor: هذا احتجاج على العالم بالبداءة الأولى

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan reads al-baʿth with an open ʿayn; Basrans call it a dialect form, while Kufans analyze it as a lightened form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن «البعث» بفتح العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from soil refers to the creation of Adam, the origin of humanity.
rows.anchor: أي خلقنا أباكم الذي هو أصل البشر يعني آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa is semen and takes its name from being a small amount of water, though the word can also refer to much water, as in a hadith about the two seas.
rows.anchor: وهو المني سمي نطفة لقلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭf can mean drops; naṭafa is to drip, and layla naṭūfa is a night of steady rain.
rows.anchor: نطف ينطف وينطف. وليلة نطوفة دائمة القطر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqa is congealed blood; ʿalaq can also mean fresh blood or blood of an intense red.
rows.anchor: العلق الدم العبيط أي الطري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḍgha is a small lump of flesh, about the amount one can chew; a hadith also calls a part of the body a muḍgha.
rows.anchor: وهي لحمة قليلة قدر ما يمضغ

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The developmental stages total four months; Ibn Abbas says the soul is breathed in during the ten days afterward, matching the widow's waiting period of four months and ten days.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وفي العشر بعد الأشهر الأربعة

words: فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Umar report that when the drop settles in the womb, an angel asks God about sex, blessedness, lifespan, deeds, and place of death; the angel finds its account in the Mother Book and the person's provision, path, death, and burial place are decreed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وعن ابن عمر أن النطفة إذا استقرت في الرحم أخذها ملك بكفه

words: فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَٰكُم مِّن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: A sound report from Anas, raised to the Prophet, says God appoints an angel over the womb; at each stage the angel asks about the drop, clot, and lump, then asks sex, blessedness, provision, and lifespan and writes the decree in the womb.
rows.anchor: إن الله قد وكل بالرحم ملكا فيقول أي رب نطفة

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري
rows.claim: A sound report from Hudhayfa ibn Asid says that after forty-two nights an angel shapes the drop and forms its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones, then asks whether it is male or female.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد الغفاري قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In a sound report, the Prophet says the embryo is a drop for forty days, then a clot for the same, then a lump for the same; an angel then breathes in the soul and receives four decrees: provision, lifespan, deeds, and blessedness or wretchedness.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو الصادق المصدوق

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ibn Masud hadith clarifies the earlier reports: each stage lasts forty days, then the angel breathes in the soul, making four months; the author connects this to Ibn Abbas's account of the widow's waiting period.
rows.anchor: فهذا الحديث مفسر للأحاديث الأول فإن فيه:

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud explains embryo gathering in the womb: after the drop enters and God wills a human from it, it spreads beneath the woman's nails and hair for forty days, then becomes blood in the womb; this is the gathering and the clot stage.
rows.anchor: سئل الأعمش: ما يجمع في بطن أمه؟ فقال حدثنا خيثمة قال: قال عبد الله:

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing formation to the angel is figurative: all shaping occurs by God's power and creation; the Qur'an assigns actual creation to God and denies independent creative power to creatures.
rows.anchor: نسبة الخلق والتصوير للملك نسبة مجازية لا حقيقية
